messages.subject: Warning in Stratified Genomic SEM
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am running some stratified genomic SEM, but noticed that some of the annotations output a warning that I am struggling to interpret.

For context: I am running a model with 14 traits loading into 4 latent factors. In regular Genomic SEM, the model converges with good fit on even chromosomes, odd chromosomes, and across all chromosomes. I have also run userGWAS without any issues.

I have run the same model through the enrich function and while most annotations have no warnings, 7 out of 57 baseline annotations give the warning:

lavaan WARNING: some estimated lv variances are negative

Another 15 give the warning:

lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv <http://cov.lv>") to investigate.

To see how these annotations look in the full model, I estimated some of these annotations using the steps outlined in "Estimation of Full Model in a Specific Annotation" in the Stratified Genomic SEM wiki page. The annotations with the first warning either failed to converge or had poor model fit, so I have determined that they are safe to filter out. However the annotations with the latter warning often look ok. For example, the annotation "H3K27ac.union" gives the following in the S-GSEM:

Annotation    lhs    op    rhs    Cov_Smooth    Z_smooth    Enrichment    Enrichment_SE    Enrichment_p_value    Error    Warning
H3K27ac.union    trait1    ~~    trait1    0.00E+00    0    2.7136311    0.4479648    6.53E-05    0    lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv <http://cov.lv>") to investigate.

But it looks ok when the whole model is estimated:

#create list object with V and S for H3K27ac.union_SLDSC
> H3K27ac.union_SLDSC <- list(
>     V_LD = S_LDSC_baseline$V$`H3K27ac.union`,
>     S_LD = S_LDSC_baseline$S$`H3K27ac.union`
> )
​>
> #estimate model
> H3K27ac.union_SLDSC_test <- usermodel(
>     covstruc = H3K27ac.union_SLDSC,
>     model = modelV4,
>     std.lv <http://std.lv>=TRUE
> )
> H3K27ac.union_SLDSC_test$modelfit
[1] "Running primary model"
[1] "Calculating CFI"
[1] "Calculating Standardized Results"
[1] "Calculating SRMR"
elapsed
 12.005
A data.frame: 1 × 6
chisq    df    p_chisq    AIC    CFI    SRMR
<dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
df    79.67453    46    0.001511196    143.6745    0.9461996    0.07230769

There are no warnings and while CFI and SRMR isn't as good as genome-wide fit, it still looks acceptable.

What do the warnings mean? If both warnings are not safe to ignore, is this a case where I should I throw out all results with the warnings or should I test each annotations with the error individually and only keep the ones with decent model fit?

Regards,

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Correlation matrix p-value
messages.body_plain:
Hi Laura,

Apologies for such a late reply here! The p-values for the correlations are the same as for the covariances and there are two options then for obtaining the p-values:
1. Run a fully saturated model within Genomic SEM estimating all of the correlations across all items and look at the p-values

2. Use this bit of code to get the SEs from the diagonals of the sampling covariance matrix (V), then calculate the p-values on the Z-statistics calculated as the ratio of the genetic covariance matrix over this newly created SE matrix.

# pull the SEs of the sampling covariance matrix
k<-nrow(LDSCoutput$S)
SE<-matrix(0, k, k)
SE[lower.tri(SE,diag=TRUE)] <-sqrt(diag(LDSCoutput$V))

#obtain the p-values
2*pnorm(abs(LDSCoutput$S/SE),lower.tail=FALSE)

Best,
  Andrew

messages.subject: Re: Warning in Stratified Genomic SEM
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeff,

These are great questions. I would say we are still in the phase of figuring out what warnings require filtering out results entirely. Since enrich is fixing the factor loadings from the genome-wide annotation, running the models within an annotation won't be exactly equivalent since those are going to freely estimate all of those loadings. That being said, I think it was good troubleshooting to still take a look at some of these individual annotations to ensure that model results within an annotation look relatively normal and the model still fits well.

I would say if you are examining enrichment of factor variances, the warning about negative lv variances should generally be used to prune out results as this warning indicates latent variables with variances below 0. If the warning is about lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite, I would not examine enrichment of the factor correlations since this warning often indicates model results with factor correlations > 1.

Best,
  Andrew
